department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering

deadline.value: Scholarship rounds close 2 Nov 2026, 11 Jan 2027, 1 Mar 2027 and 1 Jun 2027. Your supervisor must also nominate you for funding by the same deadline. Each scheme is open only in some rounds, and the departmental deadline applies even for Imperial-wide scholarships.
deadline.quote: Application deadlines Round 1 02/11/2026 Round 2 11/01/2027 Round 3 01/03/2027 Round 4 01/06/2027

also.quote: Applicants must also be nominated for funding by their prospective PhD supervisor by the deadlines indicated.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Contact your preferred supervisor(s) about projects and funding first, and submit the online application only after one has shown sufficient interest. Applications without prior consultation are unlikely to be accepted.
supervisor.quote: Online applications should only be submitted after the potential academic supervisor has expressed sufficient interest in your application. | applications received without prior consultation with a supervisor or through one of our open schemes, will take longer to process and are unlikely to be accepted.

funding.value: Department scholarships are awarded by a PhD Awards Panel. One EPSRC scholarship a year covers Home or Overseas fees for any fee status; Skempton, Dixon and Women's scholarships cover only Home fees, so they give overseas students partial funding.
funding.quote: We have one scholarship funded by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC) for international candidates. These scholarships are open to all students regardless of fee status. | These scholarships are open to all applicants and could provide partial funding for overseas students.

also.quote: Submitting a PhD application via the College does not mean you will be automatically considered for a scholarship.

entry_route.value: You need a good 2:1 or first (or the international equivalent) in engineering or another numerate subject, a master's-level degree and good maths skills.
entry_route.quote: A good Upper Second or First Class Degree result (or International equivalent), in engineering or another numerate discipline A Masters level degree qualification

toefl_min.value: Non-native English speakers may need Imperial's Standard English level: TOEFL iBT 92 overall (min 20 in each section), or 4.5 on the new scale. The score can follow your application.
toefl_min.quote: Applicants for whom English is not their first language may be required to present an English language qualification, passed at the 'standard level'.

ielts_min.value: Non-native English speakers may need Imperial's Standard English level: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall (min 6.0 in each element).
ielts_min.quote: Applicants for whom English is not their first language may be required to present an English language qualification, passed at the 'standard level'.

notes: Apply to 'Civil and Environmental Engineering Research (PhD)'. Processing takes at least 12 weeks. The department also covers environmental and water resource engineering. Contact: civilphdadmin@imperial.ac.uk.
